clue.text: Give a spa a bad name and elephants will enjoy it

parts.note: someone whose name is mud has a bad name
Bath is the English spa town

explanation.surface: Badmouthing a spa resort, while elephants happily wallow in something.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue's order is spa first, but the charade runs in answer order: the bad name comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: Elephants famously wallow in wet mud to cool off and protect their skin, so they enjoy such a soak.

clue.text: One who serves food outside Ulster

indicators.note: the food word goes outside, wrapping round the Ulster letters

parts.note: a meal is food
NI, Northern Ireland, is loosely called Ulster

explanation.surface: A waiter delivering dinner just beyond the borders of Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: A menial is a domestic servant, one who serves in a household.

clue.text: Separate entry into water to catch fish

indicators.note: the plunge word holds the fish inside it as if catching it

parts.note: a dive is an entry into water
the id (or ide) is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: Someone plunging into a river to grab a fish.
explanation.walkthrough: ID is a variant spelling of IDE, the orfe, a crossword regular.
explanation.definitionFit: To divide something is to separate it into parts, a verb synonym.

clue.text: A vegetable heartless lot cut inside for seven whole days

indicators.note: the cut-down lot and the cut go inside the vegetable

parts.note: a leek is a vegetable

indicators.note: a heartless word loses its middle letter

parts.note: taken as written before losing its centre
to hew is to cut

explanation.surface: A recipe in which a vegetable is cored and chopped, lasting a full week.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' strips the middle letter from lot, and 'inside' puts that and the cut within the vegetable just after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something all the week means doing it on each of the seven days, an idiom for the whole span.

clue.text: Accommodation on the danger line?

parts.note: hot can mean dangerous, as of a risky or radioactive situation
the El is an elevated railway line in American cities

explanation.surface: A place to stay that sits right on a dangerous front line.
explanation.definitionFit: A hotel provides paid lodging, so it is a form of accommodation for travellers.

clue.text: Talk food in 9 town

parts.note: to chat is to talk
ham is a food

explanation.surface: Chatting over a meal in a navy town.
explanation.walkthrough: 9 is NAVAL, so the definition reads 'naval town'; CHATHAM in Kent was a Royal Navy dockyard town.
explanation.definitionFit: Chatham in Kent was home to the Royal Navy's historic dockyard, making it a classic navy town.

clue.text: Will this society have no education?

definitions.text: Will this society have no education?

parts.words: Will this society have no education?
parts.note: a society with no social ranks, read jokingly as one lacking lessons or school classes

explanation.surface: A worried question about whether an egalitarian society would neglect schooling.
explanation.definitionFit: A society without social ranks is described with this adjective; the joke takes classes as school lessons.

clue.text: A "Y" is one also

parts.note: on a graph the vertical Y line is one of these reference lines, as is the horizontal X line

explanation.surface: A remark that the letter Y also counts as one of something.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue hints at the companion reading A-X-IS: an X is one too.
explanation.definitionFit: The Y line on a graph is a reference line of the coordinate system, as is the X line.

clue.text: Musical with a little bit to learn in a little break

parts.note: Hair is the 1960s rock musical
an actor's line is a short piece of script to learn

explanation.surface: A performer in a musical, a few lines to learn, in a short intermission.
explanation.definitionFit: A hairline fracture is a very fine crack, so the word describes a tiny break.

clue.text: Obvious person if he is translated

parts.note: a man is a person
taken as written
in Latin, est is 'he is', the pronoun understood

explanation.surface: Someone who would be plain to see if only he were translated.
explanation.definitionFit: Manifest as an adjective means plain to see, evident, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Object of contemplation heard relating to a service

indicators.note: signals that the word for the contemplated object is said out loud

parts.note: the navel is what one gazes at in navel-gazing

explanation.surface: Something gazed at in meditation, overheard while discussing the armed forces.
explanation.definitionFit: Naval means relating to the navy, one of the armed services.

clue.text: Practice established with time: it's in a way to telegraph pole

indicators.note: the IT goes in the middle of the broadcasting word

parts.note: radio is a way of sending messages, wireless telegraphy
the word it, with 's standing for 'is'
N is the north pole

explanation.surface: Over time a custom grew up of telegraphing from a pole.
explanation.definitionFit: A tradition is a custom or practice that has become established over time.

clue.text: See 25
Sign for staff of muscle formation

indicators.note: the letters are taken out of the run of words that follow

explanation.surface: A gym poster: a sign for employees about building muscle.
explanation.walkthrough: The staff is a musical stave, not employees.
explanation.definitionFit: A clef is the symbol at the start of a musical stave fixing the pitch of its lines.

clue.text: Many in the entrances left for the stage

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the many goes inside the entrance halls

parts.note: atria are entrance halls of Roman houses
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, i.e. many

explanation.surface: Crowds pouring through the doors and leaving for the stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Theatrical means relating to drama, i.e. intended for the stage.

clue.text: Direction in Sussex town: home guards (Latin, not English) are in Form I — consoling thought (25 11 for example?)

indicators.note: the compass direction is placed inside the town name

parts.note: Worthing is a seaside town in West Sussex
SE, south-east, is a compass direction

indicators.note: the household gods are put inside the shape word

parts.note: a shape is a form

indicators.note: the E for English is dropped from the Latin word

parts.note: the Penates were the Roman gods guarding the household, a Latin word
I is one, and one is A

explanation.surface: A rambling military note about a Sussex town and the Home Guard in a classroom, ending with comfort.
explanation.walkthrough: '(Latin' tells you the home guards are the Roman household gods; 'not English' drops one E from their name before 'are in' sets it inside the form.
explanation.definitionFit: The saying is offered to console someone by reminding them that greater misfortunes occur elsewhere.

clue.text: Spooner's after the drift man, hence the crackling

indicators.note: the start sounds of the two words are swapped, Spooner style

parts.note: post means after, as in post-war
James Rorke gave his name to Rorke's Drift, the 1879 battle site

explanation.surface: A tale of the aftermath of a famous battle ending in crackling gunfire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after the drift man' is post-Rorke; swapping the opening sounds gives roast pork.
explanation.definitionFit: Crackling is the crisp roasted skin, which comes from a roasted joint of pig.

clue.text: Angry as some cricketers about opening

indicators.note: the part of the word goes about, surrounding, the opening
some of the word, its first four letters

parts.note: a hole is an opening

explanation.surface: Cricketers getting cross about the opening batsmen.
explanation.definitionFit: Choleric describes a bad-tempered person, prone to anger; the old humour of yellow bile.

clue.text: Second enclosure enclosing clock-climbers climbing, for example

indicators.note: the pen surrounds the reversed rodents

parts.note: a pen is an enclosure

indicators.note: in a down clue the word for the climbers is read upwards

parts.note: in the nursery rhyme Hickory Dickory Dock the mouse ran up the clock

explanation.surface: A second pen holds nursery-rhyme mice running up the clock.
explanation.definitionFit: A specimen is an individual example or sample taken as typical of its kind.

clue.text: See 14
Where nurses may be like Christian soldiers?

definitions.meaning: on a hospital ward, i.e. at work there

explanation.surface: Nurses on duty, marching like the soldiers of a hymn.
explanation.definitionFit: Nurses work on a ward; the hymn calls Christian soldiers forward with this word.

clue.text: Monster to see shortly in Newry, possibly

indicators.note: the short see goes in the shuffled letters
the place name is possibly rearranged

parts.note: V is short for vide, Latin for see

explanation.surface: Going to Newry, perhaps, to spot a monster.
explanation.walkthrough: Newry is a town in Northern Ireland; its letters rearrange round V.
explanation.definitionFit: A wyvern is a heraldic winged dragon with two legs, a mythical monster.

clue.text: Security letting craft through?

definitions.meaning: a fastening that keeps a door secure
a canal chamber that raises or lowers boats

explanation.surface: Security procedures for allowing boats to pass.
explanation.definitionFit: A fastening keeps things secure, and a canal chamber with gates lets boats through.

clue.text: Sticker went quickly into cold travel

indicators.note: the prong and the run go into the cold word

parts.note: icy means cold
a tine is a prong, something that sticks
ran means went quickly

explanation.surface: A thorn darting into frozen ground on a journey.
explanation.definitionFit: Itinerancy is the state of travelling from place to place, as by a circuit preacher.

clue.text: The poet can't decide

definitions.meaning: The English poet of The Highwayman
unable to choose between refusing and agreeing

explanation.surface: A poet who is hopelessly indecisive.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfred Noyes was an English poet; his name splits into the two answers of an undecided person.

clue.text: The explorer is game

definitions.meaning: Marco ..., the Venetian traveller to China
a sport played on horseback with mallets

explanation.surface: An adventurer who is up for anything.
explanation.definitionFit: Marco Polo was the Venetian explorer; the same name is a horseback ball sport.

clue.text: Churchill's view of 9 10, a possible clue to Moody's health — sand blasting

parts.note: rum (odd) is a stock anagram signal, so it is a possible word for clueing the jumble that follows

indicators.note: the three words are blasted apart and their letters reassembled

explanation.surface: Churchill's verdict on navy custom, plus a clue about someone's health and sandblasting.
explanation.walkthrough: 9 10 is NAVAL TRADITION. The answer works as a clue in itself, with 'rum' as its anagram signal; the remark Churchill reputedly made becomes the clue's own wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Churchill reputedly summed up Royal Navy tradition with this phrase about its grog, vice and flogging.

clue.text: See 27
Male embracing girl in church owns Midland area

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
has means owns

explanation.definitionFit: Cannock Chase is a protected heathland area in Staffordshire, in the English Midlands.

clue.text: A boy in the wrong beat the crusaders

indicators.note: the boy goes in the wrongdoing word

parts.note: a sin is a wrong
a lad is a boy
